title: feat(status-pages): API v2 and MCP tools

summaries.body:
## Maple review 🟡 **Confidence 5/10** · needs attention The probe-pulse query has no tenant predicate and its result is returned to one org, and no test exercises `freshness.state`. 4 warnings −4 · tests partial −1 · risk medium · 4/4 new units observable · 1 file not read Adds the public v2 status page and incident API (16 endpoints), six MCP tools, and binds snapshot KV/R2 to the api Worker. The HTTP surface is org-scoped and well tested, but the freshness data behind `get_status_page` is read across all orgs and reads `live` when the prober is silent. The open `McpQueryError` issues in `registry.ts` are untouched by this change. - New `/v2/status_pages` and `/v2/status_page_incidents` groups wired into `MapleApiV2` - `registerStatusPageTools` adds six MCP tools, incident tools marked mutating - `probesSeenAt` moved from `StatusPagePublisher.heartbeat` into `StatusPageSnapshotBuilder` - `StatusSnapshotsKv` and `StatusSnapshotsBucket` bound in `bindApiClients` ### Findings
🟠 Warning · F1 · probesSeenAt aggregates every org's probes, and get_status_page returns it to one tenant security · [`packages/backend/src/services/status-pages/StatusPageSnapshotBuilder.ts:383-387`](https://github.com/MapleTechLabs/maple/blob/3f431451f43fa2baf519ef547cb5fc7f3f81f662/packages/backend/src/services/status-pages/StatusPageSnapshotBuilder.ts#L383-L387) The pulse query filters only `enabled`, `kind != "heartbeat"` and the two-day `utcDay` window — no `orgId` predicate — so it returns the newest `lastCheckAt` across every tenant's monitors. `get_status_page` (apps/ai/src/mcp/tools/status-pages.ts:298) now uses it for one page, so a page whose own monitors are silent reads `live` and its `freshness.updatedAt` is another org's probe timestamp, which the tool renders as "the page's monitors last reported at …". ``` Pass the page's `orgId` into `probesSeenAt` and add `$.m.orgId.eq(orgId)` to the `where`, keeping the unscoped read only for `StatusPagePublisher.heartbeat` if the edge heartbeat is meant to be Maple-wide. ```
🟠 Warning · F2 · get_status_page reports live with a fabricated updatedAt when no probe result exists correctness · [`apps/ai/src/mcp/tools/status-pages.ts:301`](https://github.com/MapleTechLabs/maple/blob/3f431451f43fa2baf519ef547cb5fc7f3f81f662/apps/ai/src/mcp/tools/status-pages.ts#L301) `pageFreshness` resolves `updatedAt` to `Math.min(publisherAt, probesSeenAt ?? publisherAt)`, and here `publisherAt` is `nowMs` (the heartbeat `at` is synthesized and the snapshot is built at the same instant). So when `probesSeenAt` is `null` — no scheduled check in the last two days, exactly the "live checks are delayed" case the tool promises to answer — the state is `live` and `updatedAt` is the current time, and only a non-null but stale pulse can ever produce `delayed`. ``` Decide the state from the pulse itself instead of substituting `nowMs` for the publisher side: with monitored components and `probesSeenAt === null`, report `delayed` (age it out against `STATUS_PAGE_STALE_AFTER_MS` like `pageFreshness` does). ```
🟠 Warning · F3 · Incident list loads every incident of every page before paginating performance · [`apps/api/src/routes/v2/status-pages.http.ts:452-469`](https://github.com/MapleTechLabs/maple/blob/3f431451f43fa2baf519ef547cb5fc7f3f81f662/apps/api/src/routes/v2/status-pages.http.ts#L452-L469) `listIncidents` has no limit (`packages/backend/src/services/status-pages/StatusPagesService.ts:932-941`), so `GET /v2/status_page_incidents?state=all|closed` runs one unlimited query per page in the org, flattens them all, sorts in memory and only then slices a cursor page. An org with many pages and a long incident history pays for the whole set on every request. ``` Filter and paginate in SQL: add `state`/`limit`/`offset` (or the cursor) to `listIncidents` and select across the org's pages in one query instead of flattening in memory. ```
🟠 Warning · F4 · Page delete clears the slug route without checking who owns it now correctness · [`apps/api/src/routes/v2/status-pages.http.ts:253-254`](https://github.com/MapleTechLabs/maple/blob/3f431451f43fa2baf519ef547cb5fc7f3f81f662/apps/api/src/routes/v2/status-pages.http.ts#L253-L254) `deleteRoutes({ slug: current.slug })` runs unconditionally after `service.remove`, while the sweep's `cleanEdge` (`StatusPagePublisher.ts:168-170`) reads `readSlugRoute` first and only deletes when no page owns the slug. Slugs are globally unique (`packages/db/src/tables/status-pages.ts:59`), so a page re-created and published with that slug between the two calls has its `/s/` route deleted, and the publisher will not rewrite it while its snapshot hash is unchanged. ``` Guard the delete the way `cleanEdge` does — `store.readSlugRoute(current.slug)` and skip `deleteRoutes` when it names another page — or drop the eager call and let the cleanup row's sweep remove the route. ```

## Maple review

🔴 **Confidence 4/10** · risky as written

<sub>4 warnings −4 · tests covered · risk high −1 · 4/5 new units observable −1</sub>

Adds API v2 status-page and incident routes, six MCP status-page tools and the Worker KV/R2 bindings for inline publish. None of the four open findings is fixed at this head, and the `McpQueryError` issues in `registry.ts` are untouched.

- `HttpV2StatusPagesLive`/`HttpV2StatusPageIncidentsLive` expose page, component and incident CRUD, publish and break-glass
- `registerStatusPageTools` adds two read and four mutating MCP tools, drafts unless `publish=true`
- `apiPorts` binds `StatusSnapshotsKv`/`StatusSnapshotsBucket` through `StatusPageStore.fromBindings`

## Maple review 🟢 **Confidence 8/10** · likely safe to merge Held at 8 because a warning is open. 1 warning −1 · tests covered · risk medium · 3/3 new units observable Scopes the probe pulse per org, pages incident lists in SQL, guards the slug cleanup on delete, and fixes `get_status_page` freshness; adds the v2 status-page routes and MCP tools. One suggested MCP next call cannot decode. The open `McpQueryError`s in `registry.ts` are untouched. - `listOrgIncidents` filters by page and state and pages in one SQL query - `probesSeenAt` takes an optional org id, and `get_status_page` passes its tenant - Page delete clears the slug route only while it still names the page - `get_status_page` reads `delayed` with null `updatedAt` when no probe ran ### Findings
🟠 Warning · F5 · get_status_page suggests a post_status_page_update call that cannot decode correctness · [`apps/ai/src/mcp/tools/status-pages.ts:393-397`](https://github.com/MapleTechLabs/maple/blob/bdf5facd69b1ec60146298ca8d0b9de3a2ab10c8/apps/ai/src/mcp/tools/status-pages.ts#L393-L397) `post_status_page_update` requires `status` and `message` (`status-pages.ts:454-458`), but this `next` supplies only `incident`. The registry decodes every suggested call against the target's parameter schema and drops the ones that fail (`registry.ts:547-554`, `schema: spec.parameters` at `registry.ts:345`), so the suggestion never reaches the model and each `get_status_page` result with an open incident logs "MCP tool suggested a call that does not decode". ``` Either add the required `status` and `message` to the suggested args, or drop this `next` entry — a partially-filled call is always filtered out. ```
### Fixed since the last review - ✅ ~~F1 · `probesSeenAt` aggregates every org's probes, and `get_status_page` returns it to one tenant~~ - ✅ ~~F2 · `get_status_page` reports `live` with a fabricated `updatedAt` when no probe result exists~~ - ✅ ~~F3 · Incident list loads every incident of every page before paginating~~ - ✅ ~~F4 · Page delete clears the slug route without checking who owns it now~~ ### Production impact

> **`probesSeenAt` aggregates every org's probes, and `get_status_page` returns it to one tenant**
>
> <sub>F1 · Warning · security</sub>

The pulse query filters only `enabled`, `kind != "heartbeat"` and the two-day `utcDay` window — no `orgId` predicate — so it returns the newest `lastCheckAt` across every tenant's monitors. `get_status_page` (apps/ai/src/mcp/tools/status-pages.ts:298) now uses it for one page, so a page whose own monitors are silent reads `live` and its `freshness.updatedAt` is another org's probe timestamp, which the tool renders as "the page's monitors last reported at …".

```
Pass the page's `orgId` into `probesSeenAt` and add `$.m.orgId.eq(orgId)` to the `where`, keeping the unscoped read only for `StatusPagePublisher.heartbeat` if the edge heartbeat is meant to be Maple-wide.
```

> [!WARNING]
> **`get_status_page` reports `live` with a fabricated `updatedAt` when no probe result exists**
>
> <sub>F2 · Warning · correctness</sub>

`pageFreshness` resolves `updatedAt` to `Math.min(publisherAt, probesSeenAt ?? publisherAt)`, and here `publisherAt` is `nowMs` (the heartbeat `at` is synthesized and the snapshot is built at the same instant). So when `probesSeenAt` is `null` — no scheduled check in the last two days, exactly the "live checks are delayed" case the tool promises to answer — the state is `live` and `updatedAt` is the current time, and only a non-null but stale pulse can ever produce `delayed`.

```
Decide the state from the pulse itself instead of substituting `nowMs` for the publisher side: with monitored components and `probesSeenAt === null`, report `delayed` (age it out against `STATUS_PAGE_STALE_AFTER_MS` like `pageFreshness` does).
```

> [!WARNING]
> **Incident list loads every incident of every page before paginating**
>
> <sub>F3 · Warning · performance</sub>

`listIncidents` has no limit (`packages/backend/src/services/status-pages/StatusPagesService.ts:932-941`), so `GET /v2/status_page_incidents?state=all|closed` runs one unlimited query per page in the org, flattens them all, sorts in memory and only then slices a cursor page. An org with many pages and a long incident history pays for the whole set on every request.

```
Filter and paginate in SQL: add `state`/`limit`/`offset` (or the cursor) to `listIncidents` and select across the org's pages in one query instead of flattening in memory.
```

> [!WARNING]
> **Page delete clears the slug route without checking who owns it now**
>
> <sub>F4 · Warning · correctness</sub>

`deleteRoutes({ slug: current.slug })` runs unconditionally after `service.remove`, while the sweep's `cleanEdge` (`StatusPagePublisher.ts:168-170`) reads `readSlugRoute` first and only deletes when no page owns the slug. Slugs are globally unique (`packages/db/src/tables/status-pages.ts:59`), so a page re-created and published with that slug between the two calls has its `/s/<slug>` route deleted, and the publisher will not rewrite it while its snapshot hash is unchanged.

```
Guard the delete the way `cleanEdge` does — `store.readSlugRoute(current.slug)` and skip `deleteRoutes` when it names another page — or drop the eager call and let the cleanup row's sweep remove the route.
```

> [!WARNING]
> **`get_status_page` suggests a `post_status_page_update` call that cannot decode**
>
> <sub>F5 · Warning · correctness</sub>

`post_status_page_update` requires `status` and `message` (`status-pages.ts:454-458`), but this `next` supplies only `incident`. The registry decodes every suggested call against the target's parameter schema and drops the ones that fail (`registry.ts:547-554`, `schema: spec.parameters` at `registry.ts:345`), so the suggestion never reaches the model and each `get_status_page` result with an open incident logs "MCP tool suggested a call that does not decode".

```
Either add the required `status` and `message` to the suggested args, or drop this `next` entry — a partially-filled call is always filtered out.
```

> [!WARNING]
> **Draft notice tells the model to publish a resolved incident through a tool that reopens it**
>
> <sub>F6 · Warning · correctness</sub>

`resolve_status_page_incident` calls `postUpdate` without `publish` (`status-pages.ts:516-521`), so resolving a draft leaves `published: false` and `renderIncident` emits this notice for a *closed* incident. The only tool it names is `post_status_page_update`, whose statuses are all open ones (`status-pages.ts:451-454`), and `postUpdate` sets `resolvedAt: null` for any non-closed status (`StatusPagesService.ts:1106`): following the notice reopens the incident on the public page with a new update, and the closing update can never be published. Accept a `publish` flag on `resolve_status_page_incident` and pass it through to `postUpdate`, or word the draft notice per action so a closed draft is not told to reopen itself.

```
Add `publish: P.optionalFlag(...)` to `resolve_status_page_incident` and pass `publish: params.publish === true` into its `postUpdate` call; keep the notice only for drafts that are still open.
```
